item.title: SFINAE and Template Overload Resolution
item.description:
C++ substitutes template arguments while it forms function-template candidates. Substitution failure is not an error (SFINAE) means that an invalid dependent type or expression in the immediate context of that substitution removes that candidate; it does not make arbitrary invalid template code safe.

Candidate Formation and Immediate Context #

Overload resolution begins by forming candidates. For a function template, deduction or explicitly supplied arguments can require substitution into its function type and template parameter declarations. If that immediate declaration context is invalid, the specialization is discarded and another viable overload may be selected.

item.title: C++20 Concepts and Constraints
item.description:
C++20 concepts let a template declaration state compiler-checkable requirements at its interface. A constrained candidate participates in overload resolution only when its associated constraints are satisfied. Constraints therefore replace many std::enable_if SFINAE uses with declarations that expose the intended operation set; they do not prove the semantic requirements documented by an API.

item.title: C++ Template Specialization
item.description:
Specialization supplies a definition for a particular template argument list or, for class and variable templates, for a more specific argument pattern. Select specialization only when type-based dispatch is the appropriate interface; use ordinary overloads for function-specific dispatch and concepts for behavioral eligibility.

Full Specializations #

A full specialization names every argument and begins with template <>. Function, class, and variable templates can be fully specialized.

cpp 
template <class T>
struct formatter {
 static const char* name() { return "other"; }
};

template <>
struct formatter<int> {
 static const char* name() { return "int"; }
};

A full specialization is an independent entity. It does not inherit members, definitions, or default template arguments from the primary template; define everything it needs. Declare a full specialization before the first use that would otherwise implicitly instantiate that specialization in every translation unit that uses it.

item.title: Variadic Programming in C and C++
item.description:
C++ variadic templates preserve the type and count of every argument. C ellipsis functions erase that information, which shifts type interpretation and argument-count discipline to the caller. Prefer C++ packs for new typed interfaces.

Packs, Expansions, and Folds #

A template parameter pack and a function parameter pack may contain zero or more elements. A pack expansion applies a pattern once per element.

cpp 
#include <utility>

template <class Function, class... Ts>
decltype(auto) invoke(Function&& function, Ts&&... values) {
 return std::forward<Function>(function)(std::forward<Ts>(values)...);
}

template <class... Ts>
auto sum(Ts... values) {
 return (0 + ... + values); // binary left fold; 0 is the empty-pack identity
}

std::forward preserves the value category deduced for each forwarding reference. It does not extend an argument’s lifetime, so a callee must still obey its ordinary reference and ownership contract.

item.title: Go Language and Templates
item.description:
Go organizes source into packages and modules, reports recoverable failures as values, and provides reflection-based text and HTML templates in its standard library. The same design principle connects these areas: make dependencies and control flow explicit at the API boundary.

Modules, Packages, and Builds #

item.title: C++ Template Metaprogramming and Type Traits
item.description:
Template metaprogramming selects types and values during translation. The standard type-traits library supplies common building blocks; constexpr, if constexpr, and concepts express many decisions more directly than recursive class-template specializations.

Traits, Transforms, and Predicates #

Traits conventionally expose a nested type or a value. Standard aliases ending in _t extract a type, while variable templates ending in _v extract a Boolean or other value.

cpp 
#include <concepts>
#include <type_traits>

template <class T>
using storage_type = std::remove_cvref_t<T>;

template <class T>
inline constexpr bool is_plain_object_v =
 std::same_as<T, std::remove_cvref_t<T>>;

item.title: C++ Template Fundamentals
item.description:
A template is a declaration family parameterized by types, constant values, templates, and packs. A specialization is formed under C++ name lookup, type checking, overload resolution, and constraint rules; templates are not textual substitution.

Template Parameters #

Type parameters accept types, constant template parameters accept structural constant values, and template template parameters accept a compatible template. Defaults provide omitted arguments. A parameter pack represents zero or more parameters or arguments.
